_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `sourcing.curate` is a semio-NATIVE curation document composed over an `s.stdio.semio.kit` catalogue child, so no oracle is registered and the evidence rests on the three committed per-kind specification vectors plus the inverse law (see noOracleDecisions).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third party reads or writes `.curate.dsl.semio`, whose body is a composed `s.stdio.semio.kit` catalogue handle followed by two handcrafted tables. A bill-of-materials or inventory library could not adjudicate this vocabulary either, because the question it answers is a taxonomy question rather than an arithmetic one: `curated` is the ONE user-editable id-keyed collection, while `stock` beside it is a bulk-populated reference catalogue seeded from hot-installed `sourcing.module` contributions and reaches the document through `ArtifactStore::reset`, never through a mutation. That is why the closed vocabulary is exactly three kinds and not five — `CuratedItem` carries no name beyond its `objectId` so there is no rename, and no nested collection so there is no add/remove-member pair. Confidence comes instead from the three committed, independently handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, each already unit-tested inside the production crate, re-exercised end to end here through `apply_sourcing_mutation_reporting`; and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property. All three vectors are real-effect `applied` vectors against the same two-entry curation, which lets each kind be held to a POSITIONAL claim as well as a membership one: a create appends after the members already present, a delete leaves the survivor where it was, and a count change moves neither.
